subject: general
question: Which of the following approach of human development is associated with Amartya Sen?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Capability Approach**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Capability Approach** is a theoretical framework for human development pioneered by the Nobel Laureate **Amartya Sen** during the **1980s**.
 
• It shifts the focus of development from **economic growth** and **income levels** to the actual **freedoms** and **opportunities** individuals have to lead the lives they value.
 
• According to **Amartya Sen**, development should be seen as the expansion of **human capabilities**, which refers to the various combinations of 'functionings' (beings and doings) that a person can achieve.
 
• This approach was instrumental in the creation of the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, as it provided the philosophical backbone for moving beyond **GDP** as a measure of progress.
 
• It emphasizes that poverty is not just a lack of **income** but a **capability deprivation**, such as the inability to be healthy, well-nourished, or educated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basic Needs Approach**:

 
 
• Initially proposed by the **International Labour Organization (ILO)**.
 
• Focuses on providing six essential requirements: **health**, **education**, **food**, **water supply**, **sanitation**, and **housing**.
 
 
 
• **Welfare Approach**:
 
 
• Treats humans as passive **beneficiaries** of development rather than active participants.
 
• It advocates for high **government expenditure** on social sectors like **healthcare** and **education** to improve living standards.
 
 
 
• **Income Approach**:
 
 
• The most **traditional** and oldest approach to human development.
 
• It links the level of **development** directly to the level of **income**, assuming higher income allows for greater **freedom**.
